clue.text: Less on top of British tree

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

explanation.surface: Some comment on a British tree having fewer leaves at its crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less on top' reads as part of the tree picture but is the definition: having less hair on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone balder has less hair covering the crown of the head, a comparative adjective matching the phrase.

clue.text: Very dirty, sailor in game

parts.note: black can mean filthy, as in hands black with grime
Jack, short for Jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A grimy seaman playing a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackjack is the card game also called pontoon or twenty-one.

clue.text: Smallest bottom of those in final

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the other word

parts.note: last means final

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The tiniest of those at the foot of the table in the final.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, so it means of the smallest amount.

clue.text: Rough lough, say

parts.note: the two words are spelt alike at the end but pronounced differently, an example of a rhyme for the eye only

explanation.walkthrough: Lough is the Irish word for a lake, pronounced like 'loch', so it does not chime with 'rough'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words like these look as though they rhyme in print but do not when spoken.

clue.text: Offered a freer view, started shooting

definitions.meaning: spoke more frankly, revealing more of oneself or a scene
began firing, as guns do when they open fire

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: to speak or show more freely, and to begin firing weapons.

clue.text: Creature that could make monk, perhaps, sit up?

parts.note: a monk is an example of a man at prayer

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word sit is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks which animal might get a monk to sit up and take notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'sit up' is not about paying attention: 'up' turns 'sit' backwards in a down clue, and a monk is only one example of a praying man.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is an insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer.

clue.text: Gold found under an overturned steamship in port

indicators.note: in a down clue being found under puts the gold symbol at the bottom
overturned means the little word an is turned upside down in a down clue

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Treasure discovered beneath a capsized steamer in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns AN to NA; SS reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau, capital of the Bahamas, is a seaport.

clue.text: Slipping up, party to daughter's heroic action

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
slipping up is making a mistake, i.e. erring
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Making a mistake at a party, which leads to a daughter's brave exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is an old term for daring feats of bravery.

clue.text: Flat's electric current shown in diagram

indicators.note: shown in places the symbol inside the other word

parts.note: a plan is a diagram
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: An apartment's wiring appears on its layout drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat's' looks like an apartment, but 'Flat' is the adjective, with 's for 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means level, flat land without hills.

clue.text: Film, first of all, scored by American

indicators.note: first of picks only the opening letter of the word all

parts.note: in sport a side made runs or points, i.e. scored them

explanation.surface: A film whose first scores were written by an American composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of all' looks like an ordinary phrase meaning 'firstly', but it takes the initial letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus is the 1984 film by Milos Forman about Mozart's life.

clue.text: Climber in vivid red, athletic type

parts.note: scarlet is a vivid red
a runner is an athlete

explanation.surface: A mountaineer dressed in bright red, sporty sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet runner is a bean plant that climbs, so a climber in the botanical sense.

clue.text: Succeeded getting into a country, an ancient kingdom

indicators.note: getting into tells us the abbreviation goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: Syria is a country in the Middle East
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone successfully gains entry to a nation, which was once an old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was a Mesopotamian empire of antiquity, its capital at Nineveh.

clue.text: Latest in dock to carve a two-master

indicators.note: the latest letter in a word is its final one, here of dock

parts.note: to etch is to cut a design into a surface, like carving

explanation.surface: In the newest dock, someone engraves a boat with two masts.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a sailing boat rigged with two masts, the mizzen stepped forward of the rudder.

clue.text: Anxiety caused by flying to it again

indicators.note: flying suggests the words are sent scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about having to take a flight to a place once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' looks like the cause of the anxiety, as in fear of flying, but it signals the rearrangement of TO IT AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of nervous disturbance, a close synonym for worry.

clue.text: A second gamble's come unstuck at eastern meeting

indicators.note: come unstuck means fallen apart, so the word gamble's falls into a new order

explanation.surface: A second bet goes wrong at a gathering in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come unstuck' reads as the gamble failing, but it tells you to shuffle the letters of 'gamble's'; the possessive s counts as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of people or things, so a meeting.

clue.text: Sexton's article supports racists, unfortunately

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means sitting underneath the other piece
unfortunately suggests the word racists ends up badly arranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church officer's piece of writing backs bigots, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristan looks after a church's sacred vessels, the role a sexton fills.

clue.text: Motorists bypassing Greek city founded in 1566

indicators.note: bypassing pictures the outer pair going around the abbreviation on either side

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motorists' organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers take a ring road round a Greek town established in the sixteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra, the Indian city of the Taj Mahal, was rebuilt as Akbar's capital from 1566.

clue.text: Boy, a youth who drowned saving ten

indicators.note: saving means keeping hold of, so the numeral is held within

parts.note: Leander drowned swimming the Hellespont to reach Hero, in Greek legend
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: A lad who drowned while rescuing ten others.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander is a boy's name.

clue.text: Hard to stop litter-dropper with lawsuit —- one appears to advantage in it

definitions.text: one appears to advantage in it

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the letter sits within

parts.note: a sow drops a litter of piglets
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Struggling to stop someone dropping rubbish via legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter-dropper' looks like a person who drops rubbish, but means an animal that gives birth to a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a display case in which items are shown off favourably.

clue.text: Give up power

definitions.meaning: to abandon a habit, as in quitting smoking
strength or punch, as of a strong drink

explanation.definitionFit: Two idioms: one quits a habit by doing this, and a strong drink has this sort of punch.

clue.text: A short term, oddly, for a Scottish valley

indicators.note: oddly suggests the words are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: A brief word is used, strangely, for a glen in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Strathmore is the broad vale in Angus and Perthshire; strath is Scots for a wide river valley.

clue.text: Bill, having little money, shows stress

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An invoice for a small sum causes strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Accent is emphasis placed on a syllable, a sense of stress.

clue.text: Battle against royal household

parts.note: agin is a dialect word for against
a monarch's court is the royal household

explanation.surface: A fight against the king's or queen's own establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was Henry V's 1415 victory over the French.

clue.text: Panic admitted by Territorial Army

indicators.note: admitted by means held within the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: Fear felt by reservists of the Territorial Army.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer military reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fear, a synonym for panic.

clue.text: Girl with the Italian mother

parts.note: il is Italian for the
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A girl accompanied by her mother from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilma is a female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Ring worn by miss, unattached

indicators.note: worn by places the ring shape inside the word for miss

parts.note: to miss is to lose, as with a chance
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring worn by a single woman, showing she is free.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose means not fastened or attached to anything.

clue.text: Show age of hunter

parts.note: an act is a show or performance
an aeon is a vast age

explanation.surface: A display of how old a huntsman is.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Actaeon, a hunter, saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon was the hunter of Greek legend torn apart by his own hounds.

clue.text: Ordeals affected naval officer

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of the word are changed in order

explanation.surface: Hardships took their toll on an officer in the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sea Lord is one of the senior admirals on the British Admiralty Board.

clue.text: Menacing bird, blue

parts.note: mina is a variant spelling of mynah, the Asian starling
blue is the Conservative colour, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A threatening bird with blue feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Conservative party's colour is blue, so a 'blue' is a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Minatory is a formal word for threatening.

clue.text: Nothing in measuring instrument can show up sky phenomenon

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the instrument word

parts.note: a meter is a device that measures, like a gas meter
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A gauge with a zero reading can reveal something happening in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a streak of light in the night sky from a burning space rock.
